NVDA.summary: The online conversation around Nvidia right now is dominated by a bizarre and salacious rumor involving CEO Jensen Huang, and it has completely overtaken any discussion of the company's actual business. Reddit mentions exploded from 94 to 426 in 24 hours, putting NVDA at the number one rank across all tickers, and the Stocktwits feed is a mix of crude jokes, conspiracy theories, and genuine confusion. The core of the chatter is an unverified story that Jensen Huang was involved with a woman described in posts as a Chinese spy. Whether or not there is any truth to it, the market has clearly reacted: multiple posters claim Nvidia has shed nearly $800 billion in market cap since the story broke, and one user quipped that it's 'one expensive piece of ass.' The tone is split. Some are furious, calling it a 'planned attack' and an 'all-orchestrated rigged operation,' urging others to 'ignore the FUD.' Others are trying to be rational, pointing out that 'news changes NOTHING about the chips these companies NEED' and asking, 'does that really matter for this stock?' A few are using the dip as a buying opportunity, with one posting a 1,750-share position at $179.16 and cheering 'LFG.' But the sentiment tags on Stocktwits lean bearish (19 bearish vs. 13 bullish), and the most-liked messages are darkly humorous or outright fearful. One top post warns that 'this woman's cat will cause a trillion dollar drawdown in the market tomorrow,' and another jokes about never being rich enough to have a Chinese spy mistress. There's also spillover into broader ETFs like SPY and QQQ, with traders worried about contagion. For investors, the key takeaway is that this is a headline-driven, rumor-fueled selloff with no confirmed fundamental news. Nvidia's actual demand for AI chips remains strong, and nothing in these messages changes the long-term story. However, the market hates uncertainty, and a CEO scandal—even a baseless one—can trigger algorithmic selling and nervous retail behavior. The stock is likely to stay volatile until the story is clarified or fades. If you believe in the AI buildout, this could be a buying opportunity, but be prepared for more wild swings. Ignore the noise, focus on earnings and guidance, and don't let the Stocktwits circus dictate your strategy.
